item.title: As the Black Panthers turn 60, a new exhibit spotlights their Berkeley ties
item.description: The party moved its headquarters to South Berkeley in the late 1960s, a chapter recounted in the exhibit on view at the Central Library.

item.title: He proposed, forgetting they were already married. So they wed again at his Berkeley memory care home
item.description: Michael O’Reilley and Linda Feldman, both former Alameda County public defenders, said “I do” in a sunlit ceremony Saturday inside The Ivy on Dwight Way.

item.title: As Kneaded expands with cafe, plus new Mediterranean, Thai and donut options hit the East Bay
item.description: A running list of restaurants that have recently opened in Berkeley, Oakland, Richmond, and beyond.

item.title: Killer gets 8-year sentence in plea deal over 2022 fatal shooting in Southwest Berkeley
item.description: Claudel Moore pleaded no contest to the voluntary manslaughter of Anthony Joshua “Josh” Fisher III over a $600 debt. Fisher's family said they were “shattered” and that the eight-year prison sentence was not enough.

item.title: Around Berkeley: Valentine’s crafts, noon concerts, dance company anniversary
item.description: Other events include a Bridgerton and Indonesian-inspired tea experience, as well as a children's book fair celebrating Black authors.

item.title: Flock license plate scanner contract postponed by Alameda County leaders
item.description: The Board of Supervisors has questions for the sheriff about the controversial surveillance company.

item.title: City Council approves 8-story North Shattuck housing proposal
item.description: Some nearby residents wanted to block the 110-unit apartment complex, calling it a "behemoth" and “monstrosity.” But council members said they want more housing in North Berkeley.

item.title: Athletic Club sports bar throws in the towel; plus a Thai restaurant and a boba spot also shutter
item.description: It was a rough start to February for restaurants and bars around downtown Oakland, with Uptown's Athletic Club, Old Town's Attraros and Boba Binge in Chinatown all shuttering.

item.title: Laura X logró que se prohibiera la violación conyugal en California. A sus 85 años, sobrevive en una habitación de hotel en Berkeley
item.description: Nacida en la riqueza, su herencia se destinó a la creación de un archivo histórico sobre mujeres de un millón de páginas, y a una estafa Ponzi. Ahora depende de sus amigos y vive en una pequeña habitación que ella llama “celda de monja”.

item.title: The Wire: Why Jeffrey Epstein lied about being a UC Berkeley lecturer
item.description: Also: Why fewer Cal students are taking computer science and why two Cal students who developed an app to sell extra meal swipes were shut down by the university.
